stem.text: Let \( f(x) = x e^{- 15 x^{2}} \) and \( a_n = f(n) \). State the conditions the integral test requires for the series \( \sum_{n=5}^{\infty} a_n \), and use the test to determine whether the series converges or diverges.

answer_key.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges, because f is positive, decreasing and continuous on \( [5, \infty) \) and \( \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_{5}^{b} f(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{30 e^{375}} \).

worked_solution.text: On \( [5, \infty) \), f is positive, continuous as a product of continuous functions, and decreasing because \( f^{\prime}(x) = - \left(30 x^{2} - 1\right) e^{- 15 x^{2}} \) is negative there.
An antiderivative of f is \( - \frac{e^{- 15 x^{2}}}{30} \).

\( \lim_{b\to\infty} \left[- \frac{e^{- 15 x^{2}}}{30}\right]_{5}^{b} = \lim_{b\to\infty} \left(- \frac{e^{- 15 b^{2}}}{30} - \left(- \frac{1}{30 e^{375}}\right)\right) \), and the first term approaches \( 0 \), so \( \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_{5}^{b} f(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{30 e^{375}} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: limit notation on an improper integral

worked_solution.text: The integral converges, so by the integral test \( \sum_{n=5}^{\infty} a_n \) converges.

options.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges to \( \frac{1}{30 e^{375}} \), because f is positive, decreasing and continuous on \( [5, \infty) \) and \( \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_{5}^{b} f(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{30 e^{375}} \).
